newsitem.title: USA: MGI Pharma anti-tumor studies positive.
newsitem.headline: MGI Pharma anti-tumor studies positive.

text.p: MGI Pharma Inc said Wednesday that current studies show its anti-tumor drug, MGI 114, is producing positive biological effects in seriously ill cancer patients.
MGI 114 is being tested in a standard Phase I dose-escalating safety study that began December 1995. Phase I cancer studies generally take an average of 25 to 40 patients and two years to complete.
The company said it plans to begin a second Phase I study during the 1997 third quarter to collect additional data that will be used in planning for Phase II development.

In another development, MGI Pharma said it has been seeking a European partner for the drug but has decided it is not in the best interests of its shareholders to give up U.S. rights to this drug in order to secure a European partner.

"In light of MGI's growing revenues, reduced losses and continued good news with MGI 114, we do not believe it is in our shareholders' best interest to give up all the U.S. rights to this drug," said Charles Blitzer, MGI's president and chief executive officer, in a news release.
The company will continue to search for an appropriate European partner, he added.

Earlier, MGI Pharma reported 1997 second quarter total revenues (which include product sales, licensing and interest income) rose 22 percent from the same period a year ago to $2.8 million. MGI Pharma's loss for the 1997 second quarter narrowed to $822,780, or $0.06 a share, from a loss of $1.25 million or $0.10 for the 1996 second quarter.
MGI's cash position at the end of the 1997 second quarter was $14.8 million, with total assets at about $17 million.
U.S sales of Salagen tablets in the first six months are 47 percent ahead of 1996. Salagen tablets are used to treat dry mouth in cancer patients. ((Chicago newsdesk 312 408 8787))
